sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Standing Counsel representing respondent nos.
1 and 2 and learned counsel for the Gaon Sabha.

2. Instant petition has been filed assailing the order dated 02.05.2022 (Annexure No. 4) passed by the Deputy Director of Consolidation in Reference Case No. 87 under Section 48(3) of U.P.
Consolidation of Holdings Act.
3.
Facts culled out from the averment made in the writ petition are that the village in question was de-notified under Section 52 of U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act on 06.05.2000.
At a very belated stage, after about 20 years, present petitioner has moved a miscellaneous application under Section 48(3) of U.P.C.H. Act.
The Deputy Director of Consolidation has jotted in the margin of the application on 14.12.2020 for submitting a report.

In pursuance thereof the Assistant Consolidation Officer, Consolidation Officer and the Settlement Officer of Consolidation have submitted their report with respect to non-availability of the record which are in ruined condition.

sentences.text: Considering all these aspect of the matter, the Director Consolidation has rejected the miscellaneous application filed on behalf of the petitioner taking one of the ground that after de-notification under Section 52 of U.P.C.H. Act present application has been filed at a belated stage, which is not maintainable in the eye of law and the consolidation courts have got no jurisdiction to pass any order.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that even after de-notification under Section 52 of U.P.C.H. Act consolidation authorities have got jurisdiction to entertain an appeal or revision,
therefore, application moved on behalf of the petitioner cannot be dismissed on the ground of maintainability.

6. Having considered the submission advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and perusal of record it reveals that the petitioner has filed a miscellaneous application (Annexure No. 2)
intending to correct the consolidation record (land record) claiming is right and title over plot no.
319/6 area 1.97 acre, on the basis of the lease deed said to have been executed in the year 1949 in favour of his father namely Lal Chandra and one other co-sharer namely Sukhram.

It is submitted that the right and title of Lal Chandra has been acknowledged by the revenue court vide order dated 04.02.1975 passed in suit under Section 229-B of U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act.
7.
There is nothing on record to demonstrate that who was recorded in the basic consolidation record.
Counsel for the petitioner has failed to demonstrate as to whether any objection under Section 9 or under Section 20 of U.P.C.H. Act has been filed on behalf of the petitioner or not.
There is no judicial order passed by the consolidation authorities with respect to the land in question which is appealable or revisable by the present petitioner.

After 20 years from the date of notification under Section 52 of U.P.C.H. Act, petitioner wake up and filed a miscellaneous application without properly making out his case over the property in question.

This Court note with utmost surprise that how affected person (petitioner) had shown his ignorance when entry in revenue record, which has attained finality after the consolidation operation, came to this serious and dangerous consequence allegedly prejudicing his right and title over the property in question.
8. Perusal of record reveals that the land in question has been acquired in favour of B.H.L. Company and there is an issue of compensation in lieu of acquisition.
Nothing has been brought on record as to how petitioner became entitled for the compensation owing to acquisition of land in question.
Pleading as made by the petitioner in the miscellaneous application, which was filed before the Deputy Director of Consolidation, and averment made in the writ petition are vague and misconceived.
No case is made out for interference in the impugned order passed by the Deputy Director of Consolidation.
The petitioner has failed to demonstrate as to how he is prejudiced or is there any likelihood of causing miscarriage of justice to him due to the order under challenge.

No sufficient reason has been assigned by the petitioner for inordinate delay in filing the miscellaneous application before the Deputy Director of Consolidation under Section 48(3) of U.P.C.H. Act which,
in fact, is not maintainable.
For the correction of record the provision as enunciated under Section 48(3) of U.P.C.H. Act is not the proper remedy.
I do not find any justifiable ground to entertain the instant writ petition in exercise of extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
There is no illegality, perversity or ambiguity in the order under challenge.
